notes.meaning: In Bible times, goods were weighed on scales using stones as weights. A dishonest scale stands for every kind of cheating in buying and selling. People may think such cheating is small, but it is an "abomination" to God, meaning something He hates. Fair and honest dealing delights Him, because He is always fair Himself.

Pride leads to shame. A proud person expects others to treat him as highly as he thinks of himself. When they don't, he ends up embarrassed. Humble people do not think more of themselves than they should. So they stay teachable and grow wise.

Honesty leads good people the way a shepherd leads sheep. An honest person's principles are settled, so the right path is plain. He does not have to change direction every time the wind shifts. Crooked, dishonest ways end up ruining those who live by them.

The "day of wrath" means the time of God's anger and judgment, including the day of death. On that day money cannot help. It cannot buy forgiveness or turn God's anger away. Only righteousness, a life made right with God, rescues a person from death.

These two verses say almost the same thing, which shows how important the truth is. Living rightly makes a person's road smooth and plain, and it rescues them from traps. The wicked, though, trip over their own evil. They are caught by their own greedy desires as if in a snare. In this way sin becomes its own punishment.

A wicked man may have big hopes for this life, often built on his wealth or strength. Death cuts all his plans short, and every hope dies with him. It is very different for the godly. When a godly person dies, it is their fears that vanish, and their hope is more than fulfilled.

God often rescues good people from trouble. The wicked then fall into that same trouble, sometimes the very trouble they planned for others. Mordecai was saved from the gallows meant for him, and his enemy died on it. Israel passed safely through the Red Sea, while the Egyptians drowned in it.

Some people pretend to be friends but are really enemies. They harm their neighbors with words: lies, flattery, and false teaching that lead others into sin. Good people are rescued by knowledge. Knowing God, the Bible, and human nature helps them see through such tricks.

A whole town is glad when good people do well, because their success helps everyone. When the wicked are gone, people breathe easier and cheer. Good people build up a city through their prayers, wise advice, and example. The wicked tear it down with their curses, lies, and bad advice.

Mocking or looking down on a neighbor shows a lack of sense. A wise person keeps quiet instead. He knows he cannot see into another person's heart, so he holds back harsh judgments. He covers others' faults where he can and patiently bears insults.

A gossip is like a peddler who goes house to house selling scandal. He gives away secrets that others trusted him with. A faithful friend keeps private things private. One commentator adds an exception: unless the honor of God or the real good of others requires speaking up.

A nation without wise leadership falls apart. Many wise advisers bring safety, because two eyes see more than one. The same is true in everyday life. When we ask several people for advice, we hear every side and can choose more wisely.

"Putting up security" means promising to pay someone else's debt if they don't, like co-signing a loan. Doing this rashly for a stranger can crush you and hurt your family. We are God's stewards, or caretakers, of what we have. One commentator also points to Jesus, who took on our debt when we were strangers and even enemies, and suffered for it.

A kind, gracious woman wins honor and respect. Harsh, violent men may grab riches, but that is all they get. A good name is worth more than great wealth. Some read "gracious" as a woman filled with God's grace.

Being kind to others ends up doing you good, and God rewards it. A cruel person brings trouble on himself. He also makes life hard for his own family. As one old saying puts it, a fretful man "frets his flesh off his bones."

What the wicked earn is empty. It fools them, does not satisfy, and soon slips away. Someone who keeps steadily doing good is like a farmer sowing seed. That person will reap a reward as sure as a harvest.

Real goodness, not just a show of it, leads to life. The harder someone chases evil, the faster they rush toward their own ruin. One commentator notes that godly living even tends to bring health and a longer life.

God hates a twisted heart: people who pretend to be good while planning wrong. He delights in people who are honest and sincere through and through. They are the same on the inside as they look on the outside.

The Hebrew words are literally "hand to hand." Some take this as a handshake promise: be sure of it. Older translations read "though hand join in hand." This means that even when the wicked band together, they will not escape. Either way, punishment is certain for the wicked, while the children of the righteous are kept safe.

Nose rings were common jewelry in Bible lands. Picture one on a pig rooting in the mud! A beautiful woman without good sense and modesty is just as out of place. Beauty is a real gift, but it is wasted without wisdom. The same is true of every other gift.
Good people want only good, for others and for themselves, and their hopes end in blessing. The wicked hope for harm to others. In the end that harm comes back on them as God's anger.

A person who gives freely often ends up with more, the way seed grows when it is scattered. God blesses the giving hand. Holding back what is right brings loss. That includes failing to pay debts, help the poor, or provide for your family. However much you save, it comes to nothing if God does not bless it.

A generous person is literally a "soul of blessing," someone who brings blessing to others. Such a person will be richly blessed in body and spirit. Whoever waters others will be watered by God, like dry ground after rain. As Jesus said, it is more blessed to give than to receive.

Picture someone who stores up grain during a shortage, waiting for prices to climb even higher. People rightly curse him. The one who sells at a fair price to those in need is blessed. God's gifts are not meant to be hoarded only for our own profit.

The picture is of someone who gets up early to look for ways to do good. Such a person wins favor with God and with people. Whoever plots harm for others will find that the harm comes back on him. If we are not doing good, we are doing hurt.

Trusting in money is like leaning on a broken reed that snaps and stabs your hand. The rich who trust in riches wither like a dead tree. The righteous stay green and keep sprouting new leaves. One commentator sees here believers who are joined to Christ and bear fruit.

A person can bring trouble on their own family through stinginess, greed, or wasteful living. In the end they "inherit the wind": nothing they can hold on to. A fool who handles life carelessly ends up working for the wise.

The "fruit" of good people is their words and their way of life. It is like the tree of life in Eden, giving life and strength to others. Those who are wise win people over to God, like the "fishers of men" Jesus spoke of. Winning people takes wisdom, and doing it shows wisdom.

Some take this to mean that God corrects even good people for their sins in this life, so the wicked will surely be punished. Others take it to mean that God rewards the righteous and punishes the wicked, partly even here on earth. Either way, the wicked will not escape. An ancient Greek translation reads "If the righteous are scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?" Peter quotes this in 1 Peter 4:18.
